articles.title: Nandamuri Balakrishna, Sunny Deol, Nayanthara Lead Zee Studios’ Multilingual 2026-27 Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: India’s Zee Studios has unveiled a diversified multilingual, multi-genre content slate for 2026-27, spanning Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Gujarati and Kannada cinema.
body: The portfolio brings together commercial entertainers, action spectacles, thrillers, mythology-driven epics and regionally rooted stories.

In the Tamil language, the studio is backing “Hi,” starring Nayanthara and Kavin and directed by Vishnu Edavan, and “Sathyavan Savithri,” starring Keerthy Suresh and Mysskin and directed by Praveen S. Vijaay. The Kannada-language entry “Anna From Mexico” stars Dhananjaya, Reeshma Nanaiah, Umashree, Rangayana Raghu and Sadhu Kokila under director Shankar Guru. Zee Studios has also stepped into the Gujarati-language market with “Tom and Cherry,” starring Siddharth Randeria and Dhanya Doshi and directed by Dharmessh Mehta.

Marathi-language cinema forms another pillar of the strategy, building on the Indian National Film Award-winning “Aatmapamphlet.” The new slate includes “Jhep,” directed by Priyadarshan Jadhav; “Phulwara,” starring Priyadarshini Indalkar and directed by Ravi Jadhav; “Jogai,” starring Jitendra Joshi and Sajiri Joshi and directed by Vishal Modhave; and “Maan.”
The genre mix extends further with “Silaa,” starring Harshvardhan Rane, Sadia Khateeb and Karanveer Mehra and directed by Omung Kumar.

articles.title: Hulu Cancels Mindy Kaling-Created Comedy ‘Not Suitable for Work’ After One Season (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Hulu will not be moving forward on a second season of its recent comedy “Not Suitable for Work,” from creator Mindy Kaling. The series, which Kaling executive produced with showrunner Charlie Grandy and 3 Arts Entertainment’s Howard Klein, launched in June and ran for nine episodes. Warner Bros.
body: Ella Hunt, Avantika, Will Angus, Jack Martin, Nicholas Duvernay and Jay Ellis star in the series, which per the show’s logline, centers on “work-obsessed 20-somethings striving for professional success and, if they have time, personal happiness in Manhattan’s most glamorous neighborhood, Murray Hill.”

The series stars Hunt as AJ, an investment banker from Boston, who moves to New York for a new job and begins living with her best friend, aspiring celebrity stylist Abby (played by Avantika). They live across the hall from male best friends Davis (Will Angus), who is AJ’s co-worker and has a crush on her; nepo-baby/young journalist Josh (Jack Martin); and aspiring actor/med school dropout Kel (Nicholas Duvernay).
“Not Suitable for Work” was produced under Kaling’s Kaling International label in association with Warner Bros. Television, where both Kaling and Grandy hold overall deals.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Sings Mashup of ‘All Too Well,’ ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ and ‘August’ in Grammy Museum Video
articles.summary: Most Taylor Swift fans probably do not think of the sad events of “All Too Well” and the ultimately happy “Toy Story 5” as occurring in the same cinematic or musical universe.
body: The singer is also seen discussing her creative thought process on albums like 'Speak Now' and 'Reputation' in the 42-minute Q&A preceding the surprise performance.

Swift introduced the six-minute solo piano performance following a 42-minute interview with Recording Academy chief Harvey Mason Jr. Speaking directly to the audience, she explained that what they were about to hear would be an echo of the surprise medleys she performed on her record-breaking stadium tour that wrapped up in December 2024.

“I Knew It, I Knew You” continues to do well on the country chart — as well as on Billboard’s Hot 100 — and Swift spoke about resuming her romance with the genre that brought her to the dance. “I think this can happen as you grow up,” she told Mason, prior to moving to the piano. “I love my country roots more and more, the further along this path I get, and I want to honor them more and more, and I feel more tied and more loyal to them. The people that shaped who I am as an artist and as a writer, that all happened in Nashville.”

articles.title: Guardian-produced Gaza documentary from Oscar-winning Israeli directors of No Other Land to screen at Venice film festival
articles.summary: Film directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, co-directors of No Other Land along with Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, investigates ‘Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians’ during the war.
body: A new documentary about Israel’s bombing campaign in Gaza, directed by Oscar-winning directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, is to receive its world premiere at the Venice film festival.

The film, called NAZA, has been produced with Jim Wilson and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer, the team behind The Zone of Interest, and is the only documentary that will compete this year for Venice’s prestigious Golden Lion.
Abraham and Szor are the two Israeli directors of the four behind No Other Land, which won the Oscar for best documentary in 2025.

Announcing the news, the film-makers said: “Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.”

articles.title: Post your questions for Alex Winter
articles.summary: The 80s icon and star of The Lost Boys and Bill & Ted has also had a storied career behind the camera and on stage. Now, he’ll answer your (non-bogus) questions. You probably still think of Alex Winter as Kiefer Sutherland’s bloodsucking, peroxide-haired vampire biker mate Marko in 1987’s The Lost…
body: But Winter actually started out as a child actor on Broadway, appearing in The King and I with Yul Brynner before making his big-screen debut opposite Charles Bronson in 1985’s Death Wish 3. As well as the above, he played poet and physician John William Polidori in 1988’s Haunted Summer, and co-wrote, co-directed and starred in the 1993 cult comedy Freaked.

Since then, Winter has mainly been behind the camera: he wrote and directed the well-received psychological thriller Fever, starring ET the Extra-Terrestrial’s Henry Thomas, in 1999, and has made documentaries on everything from the dark web to child stardom and Frank Zappa. In 2020, he reunited with his old buddy Reeves for a third Bill & Ted film; and then reunited with him again in 2025, playing Vladimir opposite Reeves’s Estragon in Waiting for Godot on Broadway.
points: The 80s icon and star of The Lost Boys and Bill & Ted has also had a storied career behind the camera and on stage.

articles.title: Kit Harington joins HBO's Harry Potter series as Gilderoy Lockhart
articles.summary: The role marks Harington's third collaboration with HBO, after starring in the tentpole Game of Thrones and financial drama The Industry.
body: Kit Harington has been tapped to join the highly anticipated Harry Potter TV series as the wizarding world's celebrity-turned-Hogwarts instructor Gilderoy Lockhart, HBO confirmed to the BBC.
Harington is replacing actor Nicholas Hoult who could not film season two of the series due to a scheduling conflict.

Best known for playing Jon Snow for eight seasons in the award-winning series Game of Thrones, Harington also appears in the BBC and HBO financial drama Industry. The casting marks the English actor's third collaboration with the American network and streamer.
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone is due to premiere on Christmas this year on HBO Max.

articles.title: Manga-inspired theme park to be built near Paris
articles.summary: The construction of three new parks was given the green light after a €6bn investment from Saudi Arabia.
body: Three theme parks will be built near Paris as part of a €6bn (£5.13bn) deal agreed between France and Saudi Arabia.
The new development is expected to include a manga-themed park, inspired by the popular Japanese franchise Dragon Ball Z.
French President Emmanuel Macron hailed the move as on a scale not seen "since Disneyland Paris", and added "you know my interest for manga".
An opening date for the parks - which will be built near Cergy-Pontoise - has not been set by the Élysée Palace, but they will open in stages and construction is expected to take years.

articles.title: The Visitor review – existential Lithuania-set homecoming drama leaves everything in limbo
articles.summary: This portrait by Vytautas Katkus of a man contemplating his recent fatherhood and his own father is steeped in ennui and ends up drifting. At one point in this Nordic-Baltic homecoming film, Danielius (Darius Šilėnas) refuses an invite for beachfront karaoke, preferring to watch from behind a…
body: Little tangible is disclosed. Danielius is a thirtysomething father who skipped the funeral of his own dad the year before. Preparing the flat to go on the market, he walks the dog of his neighbour, Vismante (Vismantė Ruzgaitė), hangs speculatively at beach gatherings and falls asleep in pine forests. Ice-cream is eaten at every available opportunity. He’s not alienated exactly, but somewhat out of step. As he looks for new anchorage, even the film seems to question whether Danielius has sufficient main character energy: it periodically drifts to follow another resident, Tomas (Rokas Siaurusaitis), who is caring for his grandmother over the way.

articles.title: Charity? Acting? The Cotswolds? What will Harry and Meghan's UK life look like?
articles.summary: The couple's return to the UK is imminent - and what they'll be focusing on here is gradually becoming clearer.
body: Within the next few days, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their two children will have departed California and become residents of the UK.
Since news broke of the move, there has been some confusion as to what British life for Harry and Meghan will look like - but a picture is emerging of the family's priorities.

Over the weekend, there was a deluge of stories about Meghan's return to acting with speculation she would have a role in the next series of The Gentlemen on Netflix, created by British director Guy Ritchie.

Talks are still said to be in the early stages and we understand filming for the third series of the show is imminent - but Netflix has made no comment on who will star, leaving the way open for a former working member of the royal family with an acting background to be cast.

articles.title: Marching in the Dark review – rural Indian widows show stunning resilience as they battle poverty and taboos
articles.summary: Kinshuk Surjan’s documentary follows women in dire financial straits whose bereavement compounds their social plight, which they confront together. Out in rural India, a crisis casts a dark cloud over the seemingly tranquil vistas of wheat fields and soy farms.
body: Sanjivani, a woman in her 30s, is one such case. Eight years after her husband killed himself, she has taken over some of the farming responsibilities, along with other odd jobs, to provide for her two children. The camera rarely finds her at rest; Sanjivani not only works in the fields but also performs domestic labour for her extended family – cooking, cleaning and doing laundry. Her resilience is stunning to witness, but even more impressive is the emotional support provided by a tight-knit network of other widows. Together, the women gather for counselling sessions where they can freely discuss their emotional, physical and financial issues.
